title: Superconducting dome due to the Fano-Feshbach shape resonance in artificial high-Tc superlattices
authors: Gaetano Campi, Andrea Alimenti, Danielle Villa, G. Alexander Smith, Fedor F. Balakirev, Luis Balicas, Andrea Perali, Sergio Caprara, Gennady Logvenov, Antonio Bianconi1
abstract: In this work we provide compelling experimental validation of the Bianconi Perali Valletta (BPV) theory predicting a superconducting dome based on a quantum material design of Artificial High TC Superlattices (AHTS) made with a selected nanoscale heterostructure geometry. These AHTS are SNSN superlattices of quantum wells of period d, composed of first units, superconducting doped Mott insulator layers with Rashba spin orbit coupling (S) of thickness L, intercalated by second units, normal metal spacers (N). In these superlattices, grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), the experimental superconducting dome is obtained by material quantum design changing the chemical potential via the quantum geometrical factor L/d which tunes the Fano-Feshbach shape resonance in the pair transfer between superconducting gaps in the BCS regime and different gaps in the BEC-BCS crossover. Here we present a systematic magneto-transport study of AHTS artificial superlattices across the full doping range of the superconducting dome, from the deeply underdoped to the overdoped regime, using pulsed magnetic fields up to 72 T. By varying the L/d ratio, we tune the effective hole concentration delta=0.45(1-L/d) and map the evolution of the resistive transitions, the upper critical magnetic field and the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length
summary: The research experimentally validates a theory predicting superconducting domes in artificial high-Tc superlattices by tuning the material structure's geometry. Using pulsed magnetotransport measurements, the authors map out how changing the lattice period tunes the system through different electronic regimes, confirming predictions related to Fano-Feshbach resonances and BEC-BCS crossover physics.
main_problem: To experimentally validate the Bianconi Perali Valletta (BPV) theory predicting a superconducting dome based on quantum material design in Artificial High-Tc Superlattices (AHTS).
main_result: The study confirms the theoretical prediction of a superconducting dome, showing that both $T_C$ and $\mu_0H_{C2}$ peak at specific geometrical ratios ($L/d \approx 0.75$), consistent with a BEC-to-BCS crossover driven by Fano-Feshbach resonance.
method: Systematic magneto-transport measurements were performed on AHTS across the full doping range using pulsed magnetic fields up to 72 T.
model_or_system: The system consists of Artificial High-Tc Superlattices (AHTS) formed by alternating superconducting doped Mott insulator layers ($	ext{LCO}$) and normal metal spacers ($	ext{LSCO}$). The structure's electronic properties are tuned by the geometrical factor $L/d$.
key_observables: Resistive transitions, upper critical magnetic field ($\mu_0	ext{H}_{C2}(T)$), Ginzburg-Landau coherence length ($\xi_0$), and the superconducting dome shape.
important_parameters: The geometrical factor $L/d$, which controls the effective hole concentration $\delta=0.45(1 - L/d)$; doping levels (underdoped to overdoped).
main_assumptions: The superconductivity is governed by a Fano-Feshbach shape resonance involving multigap pairing, as predicted by BPV theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the superconducting dome ($T_C$ vs. $L/d$) and the dependence of resistance on magnetic field ($\mu_0H$), highlighting doping-dependent transport features like Kondo-like upturns.
paper_structure: The paper presents a systematic magneto-transport study, mapping out the evolution of superconducting parameters across varying doping levels by tuning the superlattice geometry ($L/d$).
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization and validation of complex theoretical predictions (Fano resonance, BEC-BCS crossover) in engineered quantum materials, bridging concepts from strongly correlated physics to measurable transport properties.
